ai.description: This 70–130 cm snake is olive-green with a distinct bright red neck patch and yellow nuchal groove. It features keeled scales and a black-bordered yellow upper lip. Family: Colubridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the bright red or orange patch on the nape, followed by a distinct black band immediately behind it, which is absent in similar-looking species.
ai.habitat: The Red-necked Keelback inhabits humid, lowland tropical forests and marshy areas, often found near streams or rice paddies at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the red-necked keelback flattens its neck and raises its forebody in a cobra-like display to appear larger and more intimidating to potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhabdophis subminiatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–15 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, often between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, the Red-necked Keelback is found in Northeast India, ranging from lowlands up to approximately 1,500 meters in elevation.
